detail.title: Path Dependence in Multi-Agent Interaction Protocols
detail.summary: This synthesis evaluates how initial communication constraints in MARL systems function as structural precursors, guiding the trajectory of emergent social dynamics. By projecting existing communicative MARL (Comm-MADRL) approaches into a multidimensional space, this research highlights that interaction protocols are not merely operational settings but critical determinants of long-term preference stability.
detail.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence analysis regarding MARL communication architectures.
